page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory density of 16.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 472 GB NVMe SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are more constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3990.17, and the uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is 37.14 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, which assist in localized vector and matrix calculations.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the E8-4ds_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and text processing tasks, as evidenced by its strong Geekbench text processing score of 2554.0 and average Passmark database operations score of 2890.86. Conversely, it is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded computing, software compilation, or medium-to-large scale LLM inference due to its lower multi-core benchmark ratings.
